ai.description: McMahon’s desert viper reaches 40–50 cm. It is sandy-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a distinctive, upturned, leaf-like rostral scale on its snout. It inhabits arid dunes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Eristicophis macmahoni* is the unique, horn-like projection of upturned scales located directly above each eye.
ai.habitat: McMahon’s desert viper inhabits arid, sandy desert regions with sparse xerophytic vegetation, typically found at low altitudes across the dunes of the Baluchistan region.
ai.behavior: McMahon's desert viper exhibits a unique defensive strategy by burying itself in sand, leaving only its eyes and snout exposed to ambush prey or remain concealed from threats.
ai.reproductionNotes: McMahon's Desert Viper is ovoviviparous, typically producing litters of 3–10 young. Breeding occurs in spring, with births recorded in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: McMahon’s Desert Viper occurs in the sandy deserts of southwestern Pakistan (Balochistan) and extreme southeastern Iran, typically at low to moderate elevations.
